bindings.label: 14-year-old female presented with a two-month history of itchy skin lesions located on the upper and lower extremities, thighs, and pubic area

Physical examination showed well-demarcated annular brownish plaques measuring 5-7 cm, with scaly elevated borders, a few pustules on the upper and lower extremities, thighs, and pubic area, and central clearing in some lesions
System review revealed no other complaints, and there were no abnormalities in the hair, nails, mucosal, or genital areas

The patient was treated with terbinafine 250 mg tablets and topical miconazole cream applied twice daily for two weeks; at two-week follow-up, additional lesions were observed on the lower extremity and inner thigh despite adherence to the prescribed treatment
Skin biopsy shows subcorneal pustules containing neutrophils with a few eosinophils, acantholytic cells, and spongiosis
PAS stain on skin biopsy is negative for fungal elements
DIF and serum desmoglein/IgA anti-desmocollin tests remain unretrieved at step limit
Serum protein electrophoresis/immunofixation remain unretrieved at step limit
Pathologist analysis states the PAS-negative subcorneal pustular histology and antifungal failure favor Sneddon-Wilkinson disease
Paraproteinemic subcorneal pustulosis associated with monoclonal IgA gammopathy
